Hi everyone! I'm Can Baykar (pronounced John By-car) from Turkey. I have a math bachelor's and I'm working on an educational proof assistant personal project (unrelated to Lean).

I'm a beginner in Lean, I've been pretty much only reading the docs so far.

I'm considering making a Lean library for analyzing JavaScript code. I couldn't find anything like this done before, although I may have missed something. The goal is to prove statements like "This is a correct implementation of this Lean function in JS." I have nowhere enough experience/knowledge to tackle this comfortably so I'll have to do a lot of research along the way if I get around to it.

Is anyone interested in this kind of project? Or do you have any suggestions otherwise?

Hi! Have fun learning Lean :)

About analyzing Javascript code - I believe that one needs to formally describe Javascript language (or at least some subset of it) in Lean to do that.
I would like to do such thing, too, but the learning curve is too steep for me to believe that I will be successful.

Thank you! :)

Yeah looks steep for me too, but I'm feeling optimistic, I can update you here if I manage to get it somewhere promising. I'll aim for the smallest subset of JS that makes for a nice demo.
